description: VibeCommit deterministic capture hooks. Registers the three events DESIGN.md 13.7 names -- Stop, PreCompact, SessionEnd -- each invoking the capture binary bundled in this plugin at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin, with `hook` as its first argument. That argument is what selects the hook exit contract (exit 0 on every path, empty stderr, at most one systemMessage on stdout) over ordinary interactive CLI semantics; a command that drops it runs the hook in interactive mode and feeds a non-zero exit and stderr back into the user's live agent turn. The binary is vendored rather than fetched: `npx` on every Stop is a per-turn cold-fetch tax on every turn of every session (D57 DX2). It is invoked through `node` rather than through its own shebang so the bundle does not depend on the exec bit surviving checkout and so it works where shebangs do not. Do not add a Node version check to these commands -- the client checks its own floor and reports it as a systemMessage, which a wrapper cannot do without breaking the exit contract. TIMEOUTS are in SECONDS, and every event has an explicit one because Claude Code otherwise gives SessionEnd hooks a shared 1.5s budget. Every value is strictly above the client's own 5s watchdog (DEFAULT_HOOK_BUDGET_MS), which the client requires to be the smaller of the two or it never fires: below that line Claude Code kills the process before the client can exit 0 quietly. They are otherwise kept as LOW as that floor allows, because the client's watchdog is a timer and a timer cannot interrupt a synchronous block -- on that path this number is the only thing that ends the hang, and it is wall-clock a developer waits (D56 D8). SessionEnd is highest: it settles and re-reads before sending, because transcript_path is written asynchronously and may lag and SessionEnd has no next invocation, so bytes missed there are missed permanently (D57 DX7). Stop is the tightest surface -- it fires on every turn. bin/ is committed, vendored content; rebuild it with scripts/vendor_capture_bin.sh, which records the capture commit it was built from. CI vendoring, the X-Client-Version header and the client/plugin skew check are CR-029e and are deliberately not wired here.
